question.prompt: Solve \(2x²-5x-3=0\). (Separate the two roots with a comma.)

solutions.explanation: Factoring using the cross method gives \((2x+1)(x-3)=0\), so \(x=-1/2\) or \(x=3\).
solutions.title: Factor and use zero products

solutions.explanation:
The quadratic formula uses the coefficients directly. Here \(a=2\), \(b=-5\), and \(c=-3\), so
\[
b^2-4ac=(-5)^2-4(2)(-3)=49>0.
\]
Since \(a=2\ne0\), the formula gives both real roots:
\[
x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}
=\frac{5\pm7}{4}.
\]
Thus the roots are \(3,-\frac12\).
solutions.title: Use the quadratic formula
